definitions.explanation: Paper currency. The polite prefix お is usually attached. Used in everyday conversation when referring to paper money as opposed to coins.

examples.japanese: お{札|さつ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{払|はら}いたい→払う：00535_harau⟧。
examples.english: I'd like to pay with bills.

examples.japanese: ⟦{財布|さいふ}→財布：00663_saifu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{札|さつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一枚|いちまい}→一枚：08889_ichimai⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{入|はい}っていない→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: There isn't a single bill in my wallet.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}→自動販売機：03078_jidouhanbaiki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{札|さつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}えます→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Can I use bills in this vending machine?

notes: The base form is ⟦{札|さつ}→札：02153_satsu⟧, but お{札|さつ} with the polite prefix is much more common in speech. Not to be confused with お{札|ふだ} (a charm or talisman from a shrine or temple). The counter for banknotes is ⟦{枚|まい}→〜枚：00650_mai⟧: ⟦{一万円札|いちまんえんさつ}→一万円札：26562_ichimanensatsu⟧⟦{一枚|いちまい}→一枚：08889_ichimai⟧ (one ten-thousand-yen bill). Common collocations: お{札|さつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{崩|くず}す→崩す：03919_kuzusu⟧ (to break a bill into smaller denominations), お{札|さつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{数|かぞ}える→数える：01926_kazoeru⟧ (to count bills).
